strategy.summary: Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG is a large, financially sound group-owned German motor maker (AG, Nordmark Gruppe). We are a small customer to it. It supplies two IE3 motors under framework ctr:4600070510, which auto-renews unless we give notice. The parts differ sharply in our position. On part:350011 it is sole source; the only alternative (Saalach) is far dearer, and our should-cost says the current price is below its cost. Here we depend on it and have little price room. On part:350010 it holds the major quota against Vesmo, which is cheaper, covered on material and approved. Here we have real leverage. It is also qualified on part:350012 (uncompetitive quote) and part:350013 (its earlier quote beat Saalach's), so those are award carrots for bundling. Copper is the genuine cost driver, and its rise supports more than the 350011 ask. The 'electronic components' part of its justification is weak for these motors. It habitually settles far below its ask. Its key account manager can only move within a small band, and anything larger goes to a pricing committee that meets fortnightly. Persona evidence is thin.

findings.text: Part 350010 (4 kW): Nordmark's price of EUR 239.21 is 2.1% below our bottom-up estimate of its own DE plant (EUR 244.39, no margin, ±5%). On that estimate it earns no margin on this part. Vesmo's CZ plant estimate is EUR 221.47, and Vesmo sells at EUR 225.61, so Nordmark is +5.7 to +8.0% above the CZ benchmark. The price is back to its 2023 level after −2.6%, +1.4% and +1.2% steps.

Part 350011 (7.5 kW): the letter asks +6.5% to EUR 370.96. The current EUR 348.32 is 7.1% below our estimate of its own cost (EUR 374.95), so even the asked price only roughly covers cost with no margin. The only rival, Saalach, quoted EUR 421.06 (+20.9%) in Sept 2026 and EUR 419.31 in 2024. Nordmark's 2024 benchmark quote was EUR 381.47. Economically, we have little room to push below the current price on this part.

Cost drivers back an increase. Copper is +47.7% over 12 months and sits at its 36-month peak; at about a 20% weight that is roughly +9.5 to +10% on price. Steel (PPI-C241) is +6.5% (about +1%) and labour +2.7% (about +0.5%). Total driver push is about +11% for 350011, which exceeds the 6.5% ask. Arguments that steel is below its peak are weak (only −1%) and cannot be checked. Power prices −43% vs 2022 is also not a cost driver listed for this part.

The letter for 350011 cites electronic components (+41% news). A 4-pole IE3 motor has little electronics, and no electronics driver is in its cost structure. We can push back on that part of the justification. Copper, however, is genuine.

Settlement pattern: renewals asked +3.8 to +4.7% and settled +1.2%, so the supplier usually settles about 2 to 3.5 pp below its ask. Its pricing committee approves changes above 2%. Vesmo states its material is covered until March 2027 at flat prices, which signals that a competitor absorbed copper so far.

Parts 350012 and 350013 are not currently bought from Nordmark.
- 350012: its 2025 quote of EUR 709.85 was 20% above the Vesmo cost estimate and Vesmo's price. It is uncompetitive here.
- 350013: its 2024 quote of EUR 1495.59 was 4.6% below Saalach's cost estimate and 7% below Saalach's current price. This is an opening for a bundling or award trade.
All should-cost estimates carry about ±5% error. The cost-gap findings are therefore indicative, not precise.

findings.text: Decision ladder: the key account manager can only move within 2 %; anything above 2 % goes to a pricing committee meeting every two weeks. Concessions beyond 2 % therefore take committee cycles, so each round needs a written, checkable case the KAM can carry upstairs. Two identical meeting notes confirm this.

Current ask: +6.5 % on part:350011 (EUR 348.32 to 370.96) from 2027-01-01. The letter is generic and form-like ('Dear Sir or Madam'). It cites copper and electronic components, appeals to years of reliable supply and gives no cost breakdown. Notice of 109 days meets the 90-day clause, so a procedural objection fails.

Their copper claim is real and checkable: copper notation +47.7 % at about 20 % of cost gives roughly +9.6 % on 350011. Steel adds about +1 % and labour +0.6 %. Our own should-cost puts their price 7.1 % below their cost. The 6.5 % ask is moderate against these figures, so on pure cost arguments they hold the stronger hand.

History of settling well below the ask: on 350011 three renewals averaged an ask of +2.6 % against a settlement of about 0 %; last time they asked +4.7 % and settled at +1.2 %. Prices have been flat since 2023. Expect opening-high behaviour and a settlement near their 2 % KAM authority if we offer a trade.

Financially strong and independent. AG within Nordmark Gruppe, 4,800 staff, EUR 1.38 bn turnover, equity ratio 29.1 %, credit index steady at 147, VDA 6.3 grade A. We are about 0.2 % of their turnover. There is no cash stress to exploit, and they can afford to walk away.

Payment terms are 30 days net, shorter than our 60-day standard, and we pay about 1 day late on average (62 % late, max 5 days). Cash timing is a small lever for them, not a pain point. Faster payment has some value as a trade, but our punctuality could be tightened before we can claim to be a model payer.

Operational style is formal and planning-driven: they enforce a holiday shutdown (23 Dec to 6 Jan) and require January call-offs by 10 December. This relevant when the new price starts on 1 January. There is no news and little personal correspondence, so the evidence on personalities is thin.

Our positional levers: the contract renews automatically unless we give notice by 2026-10-02, which is a credible but near deadline. Volume forecast for 350011 rises to 6,110 from 5,460. On 350011 they hold 100 % quota and own the tooling. The alternative source, Saalach, quoted +20.9 %, which weakens any switching threat on this part.

findings.text: Framework contract ctr:4600070510 covers only part:350010 and part:350011. It runs to 2026-12-31 and auto-extends by 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice. To stop the renewal, notice must reach them by 2026-10-02, so a credible exit is still open but only for days.

Prices are fixed per calendar year. Any change needs 90 days' written notice before year end. The letter of 2026-09-14 (+6.5% on part:350011 to EUR 370.96 from 2027-01-01) meets this with 109 days, so we cannot reject it on formal grounds and must negotiate on substance. No letter for part:350010 is in the evidence yet.

Other contract terms:
- Payment is 30 days net; our standard is 60, so this already favours them and could be traded.
- Delivery is DAP with a 35-day lead time.
- The quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per complaint.
- Their on-time delivery is 90.4%, below target (84.0% a year earlier), which gives a mild argument.
- Their ppm is 273, better than the peer median of 457 but up from 185.

History shows large gaps between ask and settlement:
- 2025 renewal: asked +3.5–3.7%, settled +1.4%.
- 2026 renewal: asked +3.8–4.7%, settled +1.2%.
- 2024: settled -2.6%.
They typically land at roughly a third of the ask. Net price is unchanged since 2023 (239.21 and 348.32). Their pricing committee must approve changes above 2%, so a settlement at or below 2% avoids that approval and is a realistic target.

Dependency differs by part:
- part:350010: they hold a 70% quota; Vesmo (CZ) is active with 30% at EUR 225.61, about 5.7% cheaper. Strong leverage for us.
- part:350011: they hold 100%. Saalach is qualified but quoted EUR 421.06 (+20.9%), and their own should-cost (374.95) is above the current price. We depend on them here.
- part:350012 and part:350013: they are qualified but hold 0% quota, so these are possible bundling carrots.

We are about 0.2% of their turnover (EUR 3.2M of EUR 1.38bn) and they are financially sound. They can walk away, so threats are weak; volume growth and bundling are better levers. Copper is up 47.7% year on year at about 20% of cost, which makes their claim for part:350011 credible.

findings.text: Delivery has improved: rolling OTD rose from 84.0% (2025Q3) to 90.4% (2026Q3), peak 94.1% in 2026Q2, but stays below the 95% contract target. It is above the peers' median of 84.6%, so it cuts both ways. Use it to hold the target, not as a complaint.

Lateness is concentrated on part:350010. In the last 12 months it was 88% on time, averaged 14 days late when late and was up to 23 days late. Part:350011 was 92.6% on time, up to 7 days late. The latest 350010 PO was confirmed 18 days after the requested date.

Quality is good but drifting up. Rolling ppm went from 185 a year ago to 273 (3 QNs), still well under the peers' median of 457, with no overdue 8Ds. A recurring issue is the 'wrong material certificate' (qn:20004413, qn:20004826, qn:20004918), a systemic paperwork failure. The latest QN was recharged at EUR 0 against the EUR 150 contract fee.

On part:350010 Nordmark beats the second source on quality: 180 ppm against Vesmo's 405 ppm. Vesmo is 5.7% cheaper, so Nordmark's quality partly justifies the price gap. Thin: this rests on single-digit QN counts.

The volume outlook is up and was shared with the supplier. Part:350010 is forecast at 8490 against 7890 ordered in the last 12 months. Part:350011 is forecast at 6110 against 5460 (+12%). This is tradeable for a longer or committed volume in exchange for price restraint. Part:350012 (+16%) and part:350013 (+34%) are growth parts where Nordmark is only qualified at 0% quota, which is an incentive we can offer.
Prices are flat versus 2023: 350010 at 239.21 and 350011 at 348.32, after a dip in 2024. The 6.5% increase asked on 350011 starts from that anchor.

arguments.text: Copper is the dominant cost driver for motors and has risen about 48 % in twelve months to a 36-month peak. With a weight of roughly 20 % of cost, copper alone adds about 9-10 % to cost. Our 6.5 % ask on the 7.5 kW motor is therefore moderate.

Our prices on both motors have stayed below cost inflation for years. We cut prices 2.6 % in 2024 and settled at only 1.4 % and 1.2 % in the last two rounds, far below our asks, while labour rose 2.7 % and steel 6.5-7.3 %.

Our price for the 7.5 kW motor is well below what the market charges. The qualified alternative (Saalach) quoted EUR 421.06 this September, about 21 % above our current EUR 348.32 and 13.5 % above our requested EUR 370.96.
The increase was notified correctly under the contract, with 109 days' notice against the 90 days required before year end.

Delivery has improved markedly. On-time delivery is 90-94 % over the last two scorecards, versus 81-84 % before, and our VDA 6.3 grade is A. On the 4 kW motor our ppm is 180, against 405 for Vesmo, so our quality is better than the cheaper source.
We are a financially solid group partner, with stable credit and a framework running since 2024, offering long-term security of supply.

weak_points: Electronic boards (+41 %) are hardly relevant to IE3 motors, so that part of our letter's justification is weak.
Vesmo is cheaper on the 4 kW motor (EUR 225.61 vs 239.21), has material covered until March 2027 and is already approved at a 30 % quota. They could shift quota away from us.
On-time delivery is still below the contractual 95 % target. Over the last three years we averaged about 87 %, with late deliveries up to 32 days.
We have a recurring 'wrong material certificate' defect (3 QNs), and our ppm on the 7.5 kW motor (366) is higher than on the 4 kW motor.
Power prices are 43 % below 2022 and steel is still below its 2023 peak and 27 % below its all-time high.
Our KAM can only move within about 2 %; anything above needs the committee, so our pace is visible.
We have a history of asking high and settling at about a third of the ask, so they will expect a deep discount.
We are a large group and they are a small customer, so walking away hurts them more than us. But overplaying it risks the extra volume on 350012 and 350013.
wants: A copper index clause on the CU-NOTATION in place of a fixed price; we would then accept a lower base increase of about 2-3 %.
A longer commitment: extending the framework by 24-36 months.
Binding annual volume for the 7.5 kW motor (about 6,100 pcs) and the 4 kW motor (about 8,500 pcs), or a larger quota on the 4 kW motor.
An award or share of part:350013 (our 2024 quote beat Saalach) and a fair chance on part:350012.
Faster payment (e.g. 14 days) as a modest sweetener.
Timely January call-offs before 10 December because of our shutdown.
red_lines: No price cut and no zero increase on the 7.5 kW motor; it is already below cost after copper.
No fixed price for 2027 on the 7.5 kW motor below about +3.5 % without a copper index clause.
No higher complaint chargeback or a ppm commitment stricter than current performance without a price offset.
No increase beyond about 2 % agreed by the KAM alone; anything above goes to the pricing committee.
red_team.opening: Thank them for the long partnership and acknowledge our recent on-time delivery improvement. Restate the 6.5 % on the 7.5 kW motor (EUR 370.96 from 1 January 2027), grounded mainly in copper (+48 %, at a 36-month peak, about a fifth of cost), plus steel and labour. Point out that we absorbed costs in past rounds and remain far below the market alternative. Offer constructively: we can reduce the fixed increase if they accept a copper index clause or give us a longer contract with binding volume, and we would welcome inclusion on the 30 kW motor. Keep the 4 kW motor out of the opening unless they raise it. If they do, hold the price, citing our quality advantage over Vesmo.

rebuttals.answer: We accept that copper has risen sharply and that it is a real cost driver for these motors; we do not dispute the index. Your own renewal history shows a fair outcome sits well below the opening ask, and today's price is the anchor. If copper is the real exposure, a copper-linked clause on today's base may serve you better than a fixed increase, and we are open to discussing it together with a longer commitment and our growing forecast volume.

The recent settlements were moderate, and we value the restraint. They were also agreed by both sides as fair at the time, and the price now stands where it began, so it has not eroded. Labour has risen only modestly, and the steel index, while up over the year, matters for a smaller share of cost. We are ready to recognise the real cost movement, but in proportion and through trades that help you plan.

We appreciate your competitiveness on this motor and want to keep the business with you. A single benchmark quote from another supplier does not set what is fair between us, however; that comes from your cost movement and our joint history. We would rather reward your position with planning security, a longer term and binding volume on a growing forecast than with a price pegged to someone else's list.

Agreed, the notice was given in time and we treat the request as valid. Under the clause, valid notice opens the discussion of a change; it does not fix the amount. Prices stay fixed per calendar year until both sides agree a new annex.

The improvement in delivery is real and we acknowledge it. Delivery is still below the contractual target, though, and there have been late deliveries along the way. On quality, complaints on the larger motor and repeated wrong material certificates are open points we would like to close with a firm ppm and certificate commitment. We see quality as part of the package, not as grounds for a higher price.

We value your stability and the long relationship, and that is exactly why we prefer a balanced multi-year arrangement. Your financial strength also means you are well placed to absorb a fair share of short-term material swings. On our side, we have paid reliably throughout, and we are ready to offer a longer commitment and volume visibility in return for a moderate step.

press: We would welcome a plan to bring on-time delivery up to the contractual target, together with a firm commitment.
Could you share the corrective action for the repeated wrong material certificates, so that we can include a ppm commitment in the agreement?
Looking at past renewals, we are confident we can again find a settlement well below the opening ask that your key account manager can approve smoothly.
We see good opportunities to widen our cooperation on further motor sizes if we find a balanced outcome on the current parts.
